title: What If Earth's Magnetic Poles Flipped?

scenes.text: What if Earth's magnetic poles flipped? The compass is the least of your worries.
It has happened before. The last full flip was about 780,000 years ago.
It would not be sudden. One study found the last flip took over 22,000 years.
During a flip, the magnetic field could fall to roughly 10 percent of its normal strength.
A weaker shield lets more radiation through, raising risks for satellites, aircraft and power grids.
Life has survived hundreds of reversals, and early humans lived through a short flip about 41,000 years ago.

description:
What if Earth's magnetic poles swapped places?
The field could drop to about 10 percent of its strength for thousands of years, but life has survived hundreds of flips.
What should we run through next?
